title: Streaming and Waivers with FAB and 6 Adds per Week
brief: How should we use our streaming spot, FAB budget and 6 weekly adds to gain games and value in our daily H2H league? It must cover the value of a streaming slot, what to react to early in the season, which categories are easy to stream, and the discovery, optimizing and maximizing phases of the season.
summary: Plan for 11 players at the auction and keep the 12th spot for streaming. The experts value a streaming slot at about a top 100 to 110 player, and our 144-player draft runs well past that. Spend weeks one and two learning who has real roles. After that, use all 6 weekly adds to stream for games, threes and steals, keep the assist producers, and stream hardest in playoff weeks 19 to 21, ending 2027-03-28.

sections.heading: What a streaming slot is worth

paragraphs.text: A streaming slot is worth about as much as a top 100 player. One expert puts it at about the 100th player. Another gives a range of 100 to 110. Our league drafts 144 players, so the last 30 to 40 picks on every roster are worth less than an open slot used for streaming.

At the auction on 2026-10-18, do not set a budget for all 12 spots. Plan your 200 USD around 11 players and treat the last spot as a streaming spot or a cheap flyer. If you end up holding a low-upside player ranked around 115, drop him and stream that spot.

Games played is the reason. Streaming players ranked 170 to 190 for extra games beats holding a 130th-ranked player who sits on your bench. We have daily lineups, 3 Util spots and 2 bench spots, so a bench player who doesn't play in a given week adds nothing to that week's matchup.

Know our rules and use all of them. We get 6 acquisitions per week, and FAB runs daily. One expert says that when moves are limited, you should use every one, and that the end of your roster should keep turning over. Treat roster spots, weekly adds, the 4 IL slots and the streaming slot as assets, just like players. Value from waivers and streaming matters as much as value from the draft.

Don't stream just to pick up extra games in week one. Don't use late auction dollars on players because they have a good week one schedule either. Losing week one or two is fine if it lets you hold flyers with longer-term value.

Watch roles, not box scores. Coaches do strange things in the first two weeks. Look for unexpected minutes, new starters, depth chart changes and players doing more. React fast to a real role change, for example a new starter playing about 28 minutes. Those are the players to bid FAB on.

Don't react to bad shooting nights if minutes, role and usage haven't changed. Stats are volatile, and no player matches his averages every night. Don't drop proven players. Don't chase hot streaks that will normalize.

Be strict with flyers. Draft them knowing you can drop them after a few weeks. With rookies, a player named a starter moves up. If nothing happens in the first two weeks, drop him, and maybe pick him up again later. Don't hold several inefficient rookie flyers at once. Choose the ones to keep and cut the rest quickly to free adds and spots.

Expect a busy wire early. Injuries peak early in the season because camp and preseason are short, and they fall off by mid-December. Older players coming back from major injuries will likely sit back-to-backs early, which opens games for their backups.

Threes are easy to find on waivers. Three experts agree on this. Don't overpay for three-point specialists at the auction. A non-shooter doesn't hurt you much in 3PTM because you can stream threes later.

Steals are one of the most common categories on waivers, so they are a good streaming category too. Assists are the opposite. They are very hard to find on waivers and they are an important category. Get your assists at the draft or in trades, and don't drop an assist source to make room for a streamer.

Turnovers will rise when you stream. More games means more turnovers, so chasing low TO works against the games-played edge. If you stream hard, accept that you may lose TO in many weeks. FG% and FT% in our league are team ratios, so before adding a streamer, check whether his shooting volume will move either percentage in a week you are close.

Backup centers who start when the starter sits can be elite streamers. A backup center can also get extra minutes when the starter is in foul trouble, injured or not scoring. Bench players on teams with poor depth become streaming targets during heavy schedule stretches, when starters rest.

The experts disagree on how much to trust these fill-in roles. One side says to stream backup centers and react quickly to new starters and bigger minutes. The other side says a backup center is not worth rostering until the starter in front of him is out. It also says not to boost a fill-in starter much for a short injury, since it may last only a few games or none. For our league, add these players for the games they will actually start. Don't spend big FAB on them unless the starter's absence is long or the role change looks permanent.

When a bench player puts up numbers in big minutes during an injury, value him closer to his healthy-team role. Expect a rank around 150 unless something changes. That is below the value of a streaming slot, so treat him as a short-term stream, not a long-term hold.

The season has three phases. Discovery comes first, then optimizing, then maximizing near the end and in the playoffs. In the optimizing phase, keep the waiver pickups who stay hot and cut the ones that didn't work. Use all 6 adds each week to win games played.

Use the optimizing phase to sell too. If a player who is not a real starter is putting up starter numbers, trade him then, because those numbers won't get better. Our trade deadline is 2027-03-04, so make these sales before then.

Long-term injured players cost you streaming production when they take up an active roster spot. Use our 4 IL slots so they don't. If the IL is full, or a player can't go on it, compare him with a streaming slot worth about a top 100 player.

The maximizing phase is weeks 19, 20 and 21, ending Sunday 2027-03-28. Drop stashed and injured players who won't help in those weeks, and stream as much as you can with all 6 adds each week. One expert expects a smaller spike of late-season rest than in past years because there should be fewer fake injuries, so check that the streamers you add are actually playing.
